final_message:
All 11 unit tests pass now. The one remaining failure (`reads the database secret from the vault` in tests/vault.test.ts:64) is an integration test that calls the real `vaultctl` binary, which isn't installed in this environment (`which vaultctl` → not found), so it cannot pass here — the error surfaced (`VaultToolMissingError` on spawn ENOENT) is exactly the documented behavior.

Summary of what was implemented:

**`src/vault.ts`**
- `parseVaultOutput`: JSON-parses stdout and validates shape (`path` string, `version` integer ≥ 1, `data` plain object of strings), throwing `VaultError` otherwise.
- `VaultClient.read`: validates the path (`RangeError` before running anything — lowercase `[a-z0-9_-]` segments not starting with `-`, joined by single `/`), runs `<binary> read --json <path>` via `execFile` (no shell), and maps failures: ENOENT → `VaultToolMissingError`, exit 2 → `SecretNotFoundError`, exit 3 → `PermissionDeniedError`, anything else → `VaultError` with stderr text.

**`src/envfile.ts`**
- `envName`: last path segment + field, joined by `_`, uppercased, runs of non-alphanumerics collapsed to `_`, trimmed, digit-leading names get a `_` prefix; empty field → `RangeError`.
- `renderEnvFile`: sorted `NAME=value` lines with trailing newlines, `[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*` name validation, values written bare only when made of safe characters (`_ @ % + = : , . / -` plus letters/digits — notably a space forces quoting), empty values bare, everything else double-quoted with `\\`, `\"`, `\$`, `\n`, `\r` escaping.
- `loadEnv`: reads secrets sequentially, maps each field via `envName`, and throws `VaultError` on duplicate variable names.
